_about: Authored words for the endpoint lab's SECTION MAP tab — the card's eleven ruled blocks (prisms-endpoint.json, D-015) laid beside the lab surface that answers each one. The tree, the attributes and every count are GENERATED (gen-endpoint-facts.py reads the brain map's own committed tree, which is m1-cluster.js's homes, self-proven at its generation). Nothing numeric is typed here: {tokens} are filled by the generator. The JOIN below is a PROPOSAL — authored words, never a measurement — and the page says so on its face. Plain lines follow gabe-lens plain mode and are checked by plain-audit.py.

tab.note: the card's {nBlocks} ruled blocks against the lab surface that answers each one. Clicking a block moves the bench; moving the bench lights the block. Lab chrome — none of it ships with the console.

head.title: section map
head.lede: The ruled shape of the endpoint card, beside what the bench draws for it today.
head.proposal: The pairing of a block to a lab surface is AUTHORED, not measured — it is a proposal, and the gap rows are the ones worth arguing with.

strings.sharedNote: An attribute three or more blocks need belongs to none of them, so it is listed under each as shared.
strings.leadLab: the bench moved and this lit
strings.absent: The card's ruled tree was not read, so nothing is drawn here.
strings.staleNote: The brain map's committed tree was built from an older inventory, so the blocks below may not match the ruling.
strings.feedbackWhat: a note about what you are looking at
strings.feedbackHint: the bench's state, the block it answers and the gap between them, ready to paste back with your words under it

lines: A block is a group of the {nQuestions} questions, ruled by hand; the {nBlocks} groups are the ruling D-015.
An attribute's home is the block its use weighs into most, and one that three or more blocks need is shared and homed nowhere.
The tree is read from the brain map's committed page, whose own generator proves its home rule against m1-cluster.js on every run.

acts.part: opens that part on the bench
acts.variant: opens that part and switches it to the distribution that draws the block
acts.exit: picks an ending, so every part is projected onto it
acts.path: picks a whole route and draws its record in the portrait
acts.none: names what would have to be built, because no surface answers it

join._about: Keyed by the block's QUESTION SIGNATURE, which is prisms-endpoint.json's own key and survives a reorder. Every signature must appear here or the generator stops. `act` is parsed: part:<k> · part:<k>/<variant> · exit · path · none.

Q1+Q2+Q9.says: The Data panel draws every table the endpoint touches, the operation on each, and the fate of the writes at the end.
Q1+Q2+Q9.gap: Provisions — what a dependency's own commit leaves behind — is carried in the feed and drawn nowhere.
Q1+Q2+Q9.plain: Tables the endpoint reads and writes, with the fate of each change.

Q3+Q11.says: The command panel holds one cell per way the request ends, and picking one projects every part onto that ending.
Q3+Q11.plain: Every way the request can end, and the one it is expected to take.

Q5+Q7.says: Stage blocks lay the same tables under the stage that touches them, which is the request order the block asks for.
Q5+Q7.gap: The stage spine is drawn only under the Data topic, so the other five parts have no stage reading of their own.
Q5+Q7.plain: Stations a request passes, in the order they run.

Q4.says: The Tests panel stacks the cases by the status they assert and names the conditions nothing reaches.
Q4.plain: Conditions a test proves, and the ones nothing reaches.

Q6+Q17.says: The Security panel draws the app band, this endpoint's own guards and the gate among them, in run order.
Q6+Q17.gap: Deciding branches and catches — the forks one call down — ride the path portrait instead of this panel.
Q6+Q17.plain: Checks that stop a request, and the forks that decide its ending.

Q10+Q13.says: The Schemas panel draws the request body and the response body as blocks, every field a mark of its declared kind.
Q10+Q13.gap: Response headers per ending are in the feed and appear on no schema block.
Q10+Q13.plain: Shape of the body that comes in, and the body that goes out.

Q15+Q18+Q19.says: The Functions panel draws the handler and the call tree behind it, each function marked by what it decides and touches.
Q15+Q18+Q19.plain: Code that runs behind the door, sorted by how much it decides.

Q16.says: The path record's last section names everything alive while the request runs, coloured by how long it lasts.
Q16.gap: A route must be picked first — the in-flight reading has no panel of its own.
Q16.plain: Values alive while the request runs, and how long each one lasts.

Q12.says: The Security panel carries the idempotency claim and the delivery fact as two of its one-line rows.
Q12.gap: How common a piece is rides hover cards only, and the tasks and events the endpoint sets in motion are drawn nowhere.
Q12.plain: Machinery this door shares with the rest of the app, against what only it does.

Q14+Q20.says: The head bar names the door and flies the risk flag, and the command panel counts the findings behind one cell.
Q14+Q20.gap: No panel gathers the overview — coverage per condition, the findings themselves, the endpoint's place in the app and the outside services it calls have no surface.
Q14+Q20.plain: Whole-door reading — size, findings, and the place this endpoint sits in the app.

Q8.says: The Widening panel draws the screens that fetch this endpoint and the ladder from the door out to the app.
Q8.gap: Whether the client can tell the endings apart is measured in the feed and drawn on no rung.
Q8.plain: Screens that call this door, and what they do with each answer.

feedback.lede: section map · a note from the bench
